summary:
The UN climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended on Sunday without an overarching agreement after two days of overtime. Deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming prevented nearly 200 countries from reaching consensus. European and vulnerable nations rejected a proposed deal after Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas. Australia's prime minister blamed "difficult geopolitical times," and Pacific island nations expressed despair.

Ukraine has claimed responsibility for strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya on Sunday. President Volodymyr Zelensky said seven naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at a Libyan port and also hit a cargo ship. The Kremlin warned of an "escalation of tensions in the region" but declined to comment directly on the attacks, and the United Nations called for an investigation.

Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, after he resigned earlier this month amid news of his affairs. He is suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset. U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the decision as a "correct and proper decision", and Nvidia's stock spiked 31 percent in premarket trading.

headlines.title: UN climate talks in Turkey end without agreement on fossil fuels
headlines.summary: The COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended Sunday without a final agreement after two days of overtime. Saudi Arabia and other oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, oil and gas, and the European Union and vulnerable nations rejected the draft.

headlines.title: Ukraine says it sank Russian warship off Libya
headlines.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine used seven naval drones in Sunday's attack, which sank the Russian corvette Merkury at a Libyan port and also hit a cargo ship. The Kremlin warned of an "escalation of tensions in the region" but declined to comment directly, and the United Nations called for an investigation.

headlines.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as chief executive
headlines.summary: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back Jensen Huang as chief executive, after he resigned earlier this month amid news of his affairs. Nvidia's stock spiked 31 percent in premarket trading, and U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the decision as a "correct and proper decision".

headlines.title: Indonesian candy factory fire kills 24, with about 30 missing
headlines.summary: Indonesia confirmed 24 deaths from a fire that tore through a confectionery factory in Banten at the weekend. Rescuers are searching the burned wreckage for about 30 missing people, and DNA is needed to identify victims.

headlines.title: Drones strike UN building and homes in Sudan's capital Khartoum
headlines.summary: Drone strikes damaged a UN building in a residential area of Khartoum, with explosions near the airport from about 2:00 a.m. to 4:30 a.m. The UN agency said it was unacceptable that humanitarian workers were exposed to such danger.

headlines.title: Oxfam says Israeli attacks turned Gaza into a toxic wasteland
headlines.summary: Oxfam says Israeli attacks have turned Gaza into a "toxic wasteland", with signs of possible contamination across almost all of the territory. A scientific and satellite report warns of poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air, posing grave threats to public health "for generations to come".

headlines.title: Alice Huang had contact with Chinese intelligence, New York Times reports
headlines.summary: The New York Times reported that Alice Huang, alleged to have spied for Chinese intelligence during her affair with former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, was in contact with China's Ministry of State Security until autumn 2026. The paper cited people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence.

headlines.title: US Army plans to detonate explosives in Iowa despite court order
headlines.summary: The Army plans to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives at its Iowa ammunition plant under emergency powers, despite a federal court order blocking the move. The Army says "swift action" is necessary to protect its personnel and nearby communities.
